Since the so-called "era of large model frenzy" kicked off in China's tech industry in 2023, from internet giants to traditional manufacturing, from phone makers to new automakers, the sector has quickly fallen into unprecedented anxiety. As the closest entry point to consumers, smartphones have become a must-win battleground across industries. How phone manufacturers can gain a leading edge amid fierce competition has become a new challenge. But for phone makers, competition is multidimensional—both inward and outward. Inwardly, competition among phone manufacturers has turned into a war of attrition. Beyond the usual paths of competing on specs, configurations, and pricing, vendors are now also caught in an internal race within the AI era, pouring R&D resources into capturing the high ground of "AI phones." Outwardly, OpenAI is acquiring io Products—founded by former Apple chief design officer Jony Ive—for $6.5 billion, preparing to launch its own branded smartphone; ByteDance's Doubao phone, after the first generation's explosive success, is about to release its second generation. Stepfun, Dreame Eclix, and others are also pushing into this field. Inward is a red ocean; outward is an unknown. The AI era demands new product forms to support product value. excerpt_i18n.es: A la industria de los teléfonos móviles nunca le han faltado desafíos. Sin que aún esté claro el rumbo de la aplicación sectorial, todos los sectores optaron por «subir primero y pagar el billete después» para montarse en ese «tren rápido». El teléfono móvil, como la puerta de entrada más cercana al consumidor, se ha convertido también en un «campo de batalla imprescindible» a ojos de todos los sectores. Cómo los fabricantes de móviles pueden ocupar una posición de liderazgo en una competencia tan intensa se ha convertido ya en un nuevo desafío. Pero para los fabricantes de móviles, la competencia es multidimensional: tanto hacia dentro como hacia fuera.

excerpt_i18n.en: Leiphone.com learned that on June 24, general embodied intelligence company RoboScience successfully held a general embodied large model launch event in Shenzhen. At the event, the company fully disclosed for the first time the technical architecture of its self-developed Visics large model, VLOA (Vision-Language-Object-Action), and demonstrated the model's application in multiple real-world scenarios, including the world's most complex embodied manipulation task—furniture assembly. RoboScience founder and CEO Tian Ye, and co-founder and executive president Wang Tao, provided an in-depth interpretation of the Visics large model, its underlying technical architecture VLOA, and its data system, and shared strategic plans for model generalization, scenario deployment, and ecosystem building. The Visics large model redefines embodied intelligence. RoboScience founder and CEO Tian Ye told Leiphone.com that current robot manipulation faces three core bottlenecks: poor generalization capability, difficulty in fine-grained manipulation, and error accumulation in long-horizon tasks. The breakthrough of the Visics large model lies in its self-developed technical architecture VLOA, which for the first time uses Object Trajectory (3D point cloud trajectory of objects) as an intermediate interface to completely decouple "cognition" from "execution." He said: "The word 'object' has two meanings—'entity' and 'goal'—so it precisely describes what interaction the robot body should have with an object and what changes in the object's motion state need to be achieved."

En el evento, la compañía reveló por primera vez la arquitectura técnica VLOA (Vision-Language-Object-Action) de su modelo Visics desarrollado internamente, y demostró la aplicación del modelo en múltiples escenarios reales, incluida la tarea de operación física más compleja del mundo: el ensamblaje de muebles. El fundador y CEO de RoboScience, Tian Ye, y el cofundador y presidente ejecutivo, Wang Tao, ofrecieron una interpretación profunda del modelo Visics y su arquitectura técnica subyacente V.

excerpt_i18n.es: El conocido Doubao ha cambiado. El 24 de junio, Doubao lanzó su versión profesional basada en la última serie de modelos grandes Doubao 2.1. Hasta ahora, la gente usaba la IA de forma habitual: hacer preguntas, redactar textos, corregir borradores, resumir y generar imágenes. La IA daba una respuesta, pero luego copiar, organizar, maquetar, rellenar formularios, hacer presentaciones o crear páginas web seguía siendo tarea propia. La versión profesional de Doubao quiere ir un paso más allá, para que la IA salga del cuadro de diálogo y entre en tareas laborales reales y complejas. Esta versión incorpora un modo de tareas ofimáticas impulsado por Agent, que no se limita a ampliar la capacidad de la versión gratuita ni a sustituir el modelo por uno más potente, sino que busca ayudar realmente a los profesionales.
